visual.general_description: Six-panel figure with a skin lesion photograph, three stained tissue images and two microscopy images of a fungal culture.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A is a color skin close-up of a small ulcerated crusted lesion in an orange-yellow tinted skin zone. Panel B is a low-power pink and purple stained tissue section with dense cellular areas. Panel C is a teal-green stained section with black rod-shaped and branching structures. Panel D is a framed pair of high-power stained images, purple-blue on the left and pink-red on the right, each with a thin linear structure. Panels E and F are light blue background microscopy images of brown oval cells arranged in branching chains. Panel letters are printed at the upper left of each panel; no scale bars are visible in any panel.

panels.general_description: Color close-up photograph of skin with a small ulcerated crusted lesion.
panels.detailed_description: Close-up color photograph of skin. A small, roughly polygonal central lesion has dark red to purple-red margins and an irregular surface with a whitish-pink glossy crust and a thin red streak extending upward from its top edge. The lesion sits within a broad, roughly oval zone of uniform orange-yellow discoloration against pale pink skin. No ruler, scale, laterality marker, face or text other than the panel letter A is visible, and a small blue object appears in the lower left corner.

evidence.quote: One week later (day 7), physical examination revealed a crusted, brownish nodule with raised red edges and a central ulcerated area (Figure 1A).
(A) Violaceous ulcerated lesion on the left knee.

visual.general_description: Flowchart of boxes and thick black arrows showing a diagnostic pathway for a violaceous papulo-nodule in an immunocompromised host.
visual.detailed_description: White-background flowchart with white boxes and pale orange shaded boxes joined by thick black arrows. The left box reads Immunocompromised HOST and leads right to violaceous papulo-nodule, which leads to a shaded box Dermoscopy and KOH direct microscopy above, to Punch/ Excisional biopsy on the right, and down to Cutaneous swab. The biopsy leads to Histological examination, which splits into shaded outcome boxes Suppurative and granulomatous dermatitis (arrow labelled H&E staining) and Fungal hyphae (arrow labelled PAS GMS stainings). A lower branch from the biopsy line leads to Culture in Sabouraud agar, which splits into MICs and a shaded box Dark-grey colonies and pigmented septate hyphae, and to Molecular Biology/ MALDI-TOF, which leads to a shaded box Identification of species. From Immunocompromised HOST a downward arrow leads to a box listing Total body CT scan and/or Total body PET scan and Blood culture, which splits into Negative and Positive, and Positive leads to Systemic involvement. A separate box with an orange outline reads Diagnosis of alternariosis and has no arrows attached. No patient data, values or scale are shown.
